exposure: Age of youngest child (infant 0-6 months, infant >6-12 months, toddler, preschooler)
cohort: The study cohort consisted of 4290 women from the 1973-1978 birth cohort of the Australian Longitudinal Study on Women's Health, who had infants, toddlers, or preschoolers.
finding: Women with infants and toddlers exhibited lower physical activity levels compared to those with preschoolers, and sitting time was highest in women with infants aged 0-6 months.
followup_time: Up to preschool age (approximately 5 years after birth of the youngest child)
